numeric_policy.comparison: Within each exact runtime/profile, scalar Python-vs-NumPy type, dtype and every raw numeric word are exact; input/base values, warnings/errors/events/state are exact. No rtol/atol, float coercion, signed-zero or integer-wrap normalization.
numeric_policy.NaN: Retain full raw NaN result words and all raw failures/repeats. No nondeterministic-NaN exception is admitted prospectively; any observed instability requires separate root source-contract review, not silent normalization.
numeric_policy.cross_runtime: Separate NumPy1.24.4/2.5.4 original observations. Cross-runtime type/promotion/reduction differences are retained and reported, never forced into one expected value.
numeric_policy.intersection: Exact 0/1 validation, conversion/shape/gather order, integer count and Python ratio; empty/all-zero returns Python int0.
numeric_policy.MCC: Source min comparison precedes sum; masking can hide negatives. Typed multiply and NumPy sum accumulator are preserved; zero denominator early returns Python int0, otherwise typed scalar divide.
numeric_policy.MOC: Source square in input dtype then sums; scalar sum product then **0.5 then typed multiply/sum and divide. Integer overflow, f16/f32 typed products, scalar promotion, FP stage/warning/callback order are contracts. No algebraic simplification.
